sentiment.rationale: The reported quarter includes a massive $4.5B H20 charge and a guided $8B loss of H20 revenue in Q2, making headline numbers look weak. However, the H20 charge was pre-announced six weeks earlier and came in smaller than initially flagged. Excluding the charge, the quarter was a clean beat on revenue ($44B vs $43.31B consensus) and EPS ($0.96 vs $0.93). Forward guidance of $45B absorbs an $8B China hole, implying underlying demand of ~$53B, well above street models. Management language is confident on Blackwell ramp, inference demand surge, and sovereign AI. The structural China loss is a genuine negative but was already priced in. The net effect is a positive surprise on the underlying business, warranting a score above 0.15 but held back by the ongoing China risk.

summary.eps: Non-GAAP EPS $0.81 as reported; $0.96 excluding the H20 charge vs $0.93 LSEG consensus. GAAP EPS $0.76.
summary.guidance: Q2 (fiscal Q2 FY26) revenue expected to be $45 billion, plus or minus 2%, absorbing a loss of approximately $8 billion in H20 revenue due to export controls.
summary.margin: GAAP gross margins 60.5%, non-GAAP 61.0%. Excluding the $4.5B charge, non-GAAP gross margins would have been 71.3%. Q2 guidance: GAAP 71.8%, non-GAAP 72.0% ±50bp. Working toward mid-70% range late this year.
key_risks: Losing access to the China AI accelerator market, which we believe will grow to nearly $50 billion, would have a material adverse impact on our business going forward and benefit our foreign competitors in China and worldwide.
The H20 export ban ended our Hopper Data Center business in China; we cannot reduce Hopper further to comply.
Export restrictions have spurred China's innovation and scale, strengthening competitors.
Tariff-related uncertainty temporarily impacted Q1 Pro Visualization systems.
key_opportunities: Blackwell ramp, the fastest in company history, drove 73% year-on-year Data Center revenue increase; Blackwell contributed nearly 70% of Data Center compute revenue.
Sharp jump in inference demand: Microsoft processed over 100 trillion tokens in Q1, a five-fold increase year-over-year.
Sovereign AI: nearly 100 NVIDIA-powered AI factories in flight, a two-fold increase year-over-year; line of sight to projects requiring tens of gigawatts of NVIDIA AI infrastructure.
Enterprise AI: partnerships with Accenture, Deloitte, Microsoft, Yum Brands; RTX Pro, DGX Spark, DGX Station systems.
Industrial AI: Omniverse and Isaac GR00T for robotics; partnerships with TSMC, Foxconn, Pegatron, GE Healthcare.
Networking: Spectrum-X annualizing over $8 billion in revenue; added Google Cloud and Meta as customers.
Automotive: partnership with GM; production with Mercedes-Benz starting with new CLA.
